workouts.warmup: 5 min row or bike, jumping jacks x30, hip circles x10 each, arm swings x20, high knees x20

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Controlled descent, explosive up. Fitness is about power and strength combined. Don't grind — train to feel athletic.
Rigid plank body. Full ROM. Rhythmic pace. Chest to floor. If 20 reps is easy, add a weighted vest or elevate your feet.
Pull elbows back. Hinge and hold. This is strength within a fitness context. Back strength is foundational to all movement quality.
Land soft with both feet. Reset between reps. Explosiveness is a fitness quality — train it. Step down, don't jump down from the box.
Full overhead range. Builds functional shoulder strength and stability. Athletic posture requires overhead strength.
Max effort for 30s. Alternating waves. Arms and cardiovascular system simultaneously. This is conditioning — push through the burn.

workouts.finisher: Assault Bike: 4 x 20s sprint / 40s rest — max effort intervals to spike cardiovascular output
workouts.cooldown: 5 min walk, hip flexor lunge 45s each, hamstring stretch 60s each, thoracic rotation 30s each side
workouts.progressionNotes: Get fit training requires both cardiovascular and strength adaptation. Increase box jump height monthly. Reduce rest periods by 5s every 2 weeks as fitness improves.

workouts.warmup: 5 min bike, dynamic movement prep, goblet squat x10, push-up x10, jumping jack x20

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Higher reps for fitness — keep form sharp even when fatigued. Upright torso. Full depth. Don't compromise on the last 3 reps.
Consistent rhythm. Drop to knees before form breaks. Quality reps build capacity — poor reps just create fatigue.
Move with purpose. Back pulls are as important as chest pushes for fitness and posture. Don't let back work fall behind push work.
Hip hinge and snap. Glutes drive the swing. Not a squat. Hike the bell back, snap hips through. This is the single most efficient fitness exercise.
Control the descent. Chest to floor. Stand fully. Explosive movement tests aerobic and anaerobic capacity simultaneously. Earn your rest.
Hips down. Plank integrity while running. Core and cardiovascular together. Keep hips from rising — form is the first thing to go when tired.

workouts.finisher: EMOM 5 min: Odd minutes = 10 burpees, Even minutes = 15 goblet squats
workouts.cooldown: Walk 3 min, full body stretch sequence, child's pose 90s, deep breathing 60s
workouts.progressionNotes: Track completion time for the circuit. Aim to reduce total session time by 2-3 min over 4 weeks by improving work capacity and reducing rest needs.

workouts.warmup: 5 min walk, leg swings x10, arm circles x10, march in place 1 min, bodyweight squat x10

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Establish the squat pattern. Feet shoulder-width. Knees track toes. Chest tall. This is your lower body workhorse at home or gym.
Hands elevated reduces load — perfect entry point. Full ROM is the priority. Progress to flat when 15 reps feel easy.
Pull elbows back. Squeeze shoulder blades. Back pulling patterns are essential for posture and functional fitness. Control the return.
Drive knees up to hip height. Arms pump naturally. Gets heart rate up without impact stress of jumping. Breathe rhythmically.
Drive hips up. Squeeze glutes at top. Hold 1 second. This activates the posterior chain and is perfect for beginners building lower body fitness.
Ribs down. Glutes on. Breathe steadily. Core stability supports everything — running, lifting, sport, life. Build this.

workouts.finisher: March in place: 3 min continuous at brisk pace — low-impact steady state to close
workouts.cooldown: 5 min walk, seated hamstring stretch 45s each, hip flexor lunge 45s each, chest stretch 45s
workouts.progressionNotes: Beginner base-building. Progress when each exercise feels 'easy' — not just completeable. Milestone: push-up on flat, 3x15 clean reps before moving on.

workouts.warmup: 5 min assault bike, jump rope 2 min, dynamic lunge x10 each, arm swings, broad jump x5 submaximal

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Triple extension — ankle, knee, hip. Aggressive high pull. Catch in quarter squat. Power cleans build explosive athleticism that nothing else replaces.
Load and jump explosively. Soft landing. Step down — don't jump down. Full hip extension at the top. Quality over quantity.
Strength base for power. Controlled descent, explosive ascent. Strength and power work synergistically for athletic fitness.
Full arm swing. Jump as far as possible. Soft landing. Horizontal power expression. Athletes who jump further are better at almost everything.
Squat drives the press. Use momentum from the squat into the overhead. Most demanding single exercise in the gym. Full lockout every rep.
Upright posture. Arm drive. Max effort every sprint. Anaerobic capacity is the fitness quality that separates athletes from exercisers.

workouts.finisher: Assault Bike: 5 x 10s all-out sprint / 50s rest — Wingate-style peak power output test
workouts.cooldown: 10 min light walk/jog, hip flexor stretch 60s each, quad stretch 45s each, lower back cat-cow 60s
workouts.progressionNotes: Advanced: periodise power work in 4-week blocks. Week 1-2: volume (more sets), Week 3-4: intensity (heavier/faster). Deload week 5.

workouts.warmup: 3 min row, jumping jacks x30, goblet squat x10, push-up x10, face pull x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Strength component. Hip hinge for posterior chain. Maintain flat back. This is strength training embedded in a fitness workout — take it seriously.
Bridge between strength and conditioning. Cardio through strength. Hip snap is the driver. Arms are just ropes attached to your hips.
Strength pullup — pure and demanding. The fitness community over-kips and under-develops the back. Do it properly — dead hang, chin over bar.
Squat and launch. Catch and immediately squat. No pause. Upper and lower body cardio in one exercise. High 10ft target. Keep the pace.
Strength anchor for pushing. Moderate weight, controlled effort. Fitness doesn't mean sacrificing strength — it means building both.
Drive with legs, not arms. Body leans back, then arms pull. Legs are 60% of the stroke. Consistent split time — don't die at the start.

workouts.finisher: Kettlebell Swing x50 for time — record time and beat it next session
workouts.cooldown: Row easy 2 min, hamstring stretch 60s each, lat stretch 45s each, deep breathing 60s
workouts.progressionNotes: Hybrid training requires managing both strength and cardio fatigue. Keep a training log — if strength suffers, reduce cardio volume. If cardio suffers, check recovery.

workouts.workoutName: Home Fitness — No Equipment HIIT Strength
workouts.warmup: March in place 2 min, arm circles x20, leg swings x10 each, hip circles x10 each, push-up x8

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: The movement foundation. Feet shoulder-width. Chest up. Drive through heels. Do these well and your lower body fitness will accelerate.
Plank position. Full ROM. No half-reps. If needed, incline hands on a chair to reduce load. Quality is the standard.
Hips up. Squeeze glutes hard at top. Hold 1 second. Lower back is passive here — if it fires, reset and drive more with glutes.
Get the heart rate up. Knees to hip height. Arms pump. Breathe through your nose if you can — it's a good gauge of intensity.
Step back. Knee to floor. Drive through front foot. Safer than forward lunge for beginners. Build balance and unilateral strength here.
Perfect position. Ribs down. Glutes on. Don't let hips sag or rise. Build this weekly — a strong core is the chassis for all fitness.

workouts.finisher: 30s Bodyweight Squat + 30s Rest + 30s Push-Up + 30s Rest: 3 rounds total
workouts.cooldown: Walk 3 min slowly, seated hamstring stretch 45s each, child's pose 60s, deep breathing 60s
workouts.progressionNotes: Beginner goal: complete all sets and reps with full ROM by week 3. Milestone: push-up flat x10 clean reps, plank 45s. Then progress to intermediate workouts.

workouts.warmup: 5 min row, Turkish get-up light x3 each, hip hinge drills, shoulder circles

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Eyes on the weight throughout. Master each position before moving through it. This single exercise tests strength, mobility, and stability. No rush.
Hip hinge and explosive snap. Don't squat the swing. Let the bell float at the top — power comes from hip extension, not muscle grinding.
Tall posture. No leaning. Shoulders packed. Farmer's carries build grip, core, and cardiovascular fitness simultaneously. Simple but brutally effective.
Knees hover 1 inch off floor. Opposite arm/leg move together. Shoulder and core stability under load. Humbling and highly effective.
Reactive power — critical for functional fitness. Load the hips, explode up. Land soft. Step down. Express power every rep.
KB in lockout overhead. Core fights the lean. Shoulder stabilisers work maximally. This is real functional fitness — not a machine in a corner.

workouts.finisher: Sled Push: 4 x 20m — add moderate load. Drive through legs. Conditioning and leg strength in one brutal finisher.
workouts.cooldown: Walk 3 min, hip circle 60s each, thoracic rotation 45s each, wrist flexor stretch 30s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Functional fitness progression: increase carry distance monthly, increase KB weight on swings when 25 reps feel comfortable for 3+ sessions in a row.

workouts.warmup: 8 min easy row or bike, dynamic stretching sequence, mobility prep for all planned movements

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Moderate weight. High reps. This is endurance strength. Breathing is key — exhale on the way up. Your legs will burn. That's the stimulus.
Paced pushing endurance. Don't rush the first 10. Consistent rhythm is better than a fast start and collapse. Form holds the session together.
Pull chest to bar. Maintain straight body. Higher reps for fitness and pull endurance. Adjust difficulty by foot position.
Long continuous set. Front knee tracks toes. Torso upright. Lunges for distance build leg endurance and hip mobility simultaneously.
Legs then back then arms on each stroke. Sustainable pace — not max effort. Building aerobic base is the goal here. Monitor split time.
Core endurance holds everything together. Breathe. Ribs down. Glutes on. This should feel hard by the last set — if not, elevate your feet.

workouts.finisher: Jump Rope: 5 min continuous at moderate pace — aerobic capacity builder
workouts.cooldown: 10 min walk, hip flexor stretch 60s each, hamstring stretch 60s each, child's pose 90s
workouts.progressionNotes: Endurance strength improves through increasing density. Track total reps completed per session. Goal: reduce rest periods from 45s to 30s over 6 weeks.

workouts.warmup: 5 min bike moderate, jumping jacks x30, hip hinge x10, push-up x10, 2 min easy row

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Explosive hip drive for the full 30s. Count reps per interval. Rest fully. Aim to maintain consistent rep count across all 5 sets.
Moderate weight. As many quality reps as possible in 40s. Don't sacrifice depth for reps. Safety and stimulus go together.
Chest to floor. Jump and clap at the top. Max reps in the window. This is the purest fitness test — full body, cardiovascular, and mental.
Don't burn out in the first 10 seconds. Paced effort. Keep hips from sagging. Count reps — beat it next session.
Quarter squat, explosive jump, soft land. Reset and repeat. Power-endurance — legs and heart at maximum.
Hips level. Drive knees toward chest. Fast feet. Core engaged throughout. Cardiovascular and core endurance in one.

workouts.finisher: Assault Bike: 10 x 10s max sprint / 20s easy — max intensity spike to close the session
workouts.cooldown: 5 min walk, hamstring stretch 45s each, hip flexor lunge 60s each, deep breathing 90s
workouts.progressionNotes: HIIS training: track reps per interval across sessions. Progress when reps increase consistently by 2+ across 3 sessions. Reduce recovery by 5s every 2 weeks.

workouts.warmup: 5 min row, glute bridge x15, leg swings x10, hip circle x10, goblet squat x10

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Fitness requires strength. Squat is king. Controlled descent — explosive ascent. Train the pattern that serves you for life. Take it seriously.
Hip hinge. Hamstring and glute posterior chain. Essential counterbalance to quad-dominant squat. Balance front-to-back every session.
Unilateral fitness — address imbalances. Rear foot elevated. Front foot drives. This will test your cardiovascular system AND your legs.
Power after strength. Reactive lower body fitness. Jump high. Land soft. Reset every rep. Don't accumulate fatigue — quality matters.
Hip hinge and explosive snap. Cardiovascular conditioning via strength movements. This is what fitness training looks like — not isolated curls.
Tall posture. Don't lean into the load. Core fights the weight laterally. Loaded carries build real-world functional fitness.

workouts.finisher: Squat Thrust x10 + High Knees x20: 4 rounds, 30s rest — lower body and cardio blast
workouts.cooldown: Hip flexor lunge 60s each, pigeon pose 60s each, hamstring stretch 45s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Lower body fitness day. Track total session completion time. Progress squat load when top of rep range is hit with full depth for all 4 sets.

workouts.warmup: 5 min bike, arm circles x20, band pull-aparts x20, push-up x10, face pull x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Upper body strength anchor. Chest, shoulders, triceps. Strength is the foundation of fitness — build it and the rest follows.
Upper body pull to match the push. Dead hang. Full ROM. If 12 reps is easy, add weight. If less than 8 is possible, use band assistance.
Overhead strength. Shoulder health is critical for fitness longevity. Full ROM. Keep core engaged — don't arch the lower back to press more.
Max effort alternating waves. Cardiovascular conditioning through the upper body. Arms and lungs simultaneously — elite fitness training.
Rear delt and rotator cuff health. Non-negotiable. External rotate hard at the end. Shoulder longevity underpins long-term fitness.
Plank + row. Minimal hip rotation. Core and back simultaneously. This is functional fitness in its purest form — multi-dimensional challenge.

workouts.finisher: Push-Up x20 + Burpee x10: 3 rounds, 45s rest — full upper body and cardiovascular burnout
workouts.cooldown: Cross-body shoulder stretch 45s each, lat stretch 45s each, doorway chest stretch 60s each, deep breathing
workouts.progressionNotes: Upper body fitness. Track pull-up max reps monthly. Goal: unweighted pull-ups x12+ clean, then begin weighted work.

workouts.warmup: 5 min walk, neck rolls, shoulder circles, cat-cow x10, hip circles x10

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Slow and controlled today. Recovery day is about blood flow and movement quality. Not intensity. Breathe deeply. Move with awareness.
Activate the glutes gently. 2-second hold at top. Breathing slow and deep. Active recovery restores without fatiguing further.
Slow and gentle today. Hands elevated. Controlled. This restores blood flow to the chest and shoulders without creating new soreness.
Gentle back activation. Squeeze between shoulder blades. This improves posture and counters the anterior tightness from desk work.
Inhale — arch back (cow). Exhale — round back (cat). Spinal mobility and nervous system reset. Do this slowly. This is restoration.
Light recovery lunge. Hip flexor extension with movement. Helps restore range of motion lost from sitting. No load, no rush.

workouts.finisher: Walk 5 min at easy pace outdoors if possible — sunlight and movement are the best recovery tools
workouts.cooldown: 15 min full body stretch — hold each position for 60-90s, focus on breathing and parasympathetic recovery
workouts.progressionNotes: Recovery sessions should feel restorative, not challenging. If still very sore 48h after training, add a second recovery session. Never skip cooldowns on these days.

workouts.warmup: Row 500m easy, jump rope 2 min, dynamic mobility, 3 rounds: pull-up x3 + push-up x5 + air squat x7

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Full triple extension. Aggressive pull under the bar. Catch in strong front rack. Power cleans are the most complete expression of athletic fitness.
Dead hang. Chin over. Full ROM. If kipping is allowed in your setting, strict first — always. Strength earns the gymnastics skills.
Squat drives the press. Lockout completely at the top. The thruster is both a mental and physical test — embrace the discomfort.
Full hip extension at top of box. Step down — always. Landing mechanics are non-negotiable. Never jump down from height after fatigue.
Maximum caloric output in the window. Arms and legs working together. The Assault Bike is the most honest fitness machine in existence.
Jump higher than single under. Wrists spin fast. Stay relaxed in the shoulders. Consistent rhythm is faster than forced tension.

workouts.finisher: For Time: 21-15-9 of Kettlebell Swing + Push-Up. Record time and aim to beat next week.
workouts.cooldown: Walk 5 min, full body stretch, hip flexors, hamstrings, shoulders — minimum 10 min. Non-negotiable post-high intensity.
workouts.progressionNotes: Advanced: track WOD times. Progress load on power cleans and thrusters monthly. If form degrades under fatigue, reduce load. Fitness without form is just fatigue.

workouts.warmup: Jumping jacks x40, hip circles x10 each, arm swings x20, push-up x10, air squat x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Most demanding bodyweight leg exercise. Use wall for balance if needed. Control descent. Arms forward. Build toward full ROM progressively.
High-rep fitness push. Don't burn out. Steady rhythm. Chest to floor. Fitness requires volume — earn it with quality reps.
Dead hang. Chin over. Every rep. Stop before form fails. Max reps — write it down. Beat it by 1 next week. That's progressive overload.
Explosive bodyweight conditioning. Land soft. Immediate reload. Cardiovascular and power combined. This is the heart of bodyweight fitness.
Chest to floor. Jump and clap. No shortcuts. The burpee is democratic — everyone hates it equally, and it works for everyone equally.
Core endurance builds session resilience. Ribs down. Glutes on. Breathe steadily. Increase by 5s each week until you hit 90s solid.

workouts.finisher: Bodyweight Tabata: 8 rounds of 20s Push-Up / 10s rest + 8 rounds of 20s Squat / 10s rest
workouts.cooldown: Walk 3 min, hip flexor lunge 60s each, hamstring stretch 60s each, chest stretch in doorway 45s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Bodyweight progression: track max pull-ups weekly. Once 15+ reps achieved, add weighted vest. Pistol squat: use wall, then TRX, then freestanding.

workouts.warmup: 10 min jog, dynamic sprint drills (A-skip, B-skip, high knee), submaximal sprints x4 at 70%

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: True max effort — not comfortable fast. Upright posture. Arm drive. Each sprint should feel like you couldn't possibly go harder. Recover fully.
Strength base for sprint power. Controlled descent. Explosive ascent. Strong legs make faster sprinters. Strength and speed are connected.
Horizontal power. Jump far. Land balanced. Measure distance and track monthly improvement. Athletic fitness is measurable — measure it.
Athletic fitness requires balanced pulling. Upper back strength supports sprint mechanics — posture and arm drive efficiency.
Jump feet back — jump feet forward — stand. Cardiovascular demand. Mimics athletic change-of-direction pattern. Quick feet and quick lungs.
Max caloric output in 20s. Arms and legs. Every set should feel like your first — if they don't, go harder on the earlier ones.

workouts.finisher: Hill Sprint or Assault Bike: 4 x 15s all-out / 45s recovery — peak power and anaerobic capacity
workouts.cooldown: 10 min easy jog then walk, quad stretch 60s each, hip flexor 60s each, calf stretch 45s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Sprint fitness: track 30m sprint time monthly. As strength increases (squat numbers rise), sprint performance follows. Power is the bridge between them.

workouts.warmup: 3 min bike max, jumping jacks x20, push-up x10, air squat x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Express format — minimal rest. Explosive hip snap. Breathing is your pacing tool. Nasal breathing if possible — it's more efficient.
Maintain plank. Consistent pace. Don't blow up early. 20 quality reps beats 30 half reps every session.
Deep and tall. Fast enough for cardio, controlled enough for form. This is the fitness sweet spot — effort and quality together.
Fast transition. Back work in a fitness context. Pull hard. Brief rest. This is where discipline in rest times separates fitness levels.
Finish strong. 10 quality burpees. Chest to floor. Jump at the top. These are the ones that matter most — the ones when you're tired.
Core close to session. Maintain position even when fatigued. This is where mental fitness is trained. Hold the position.

workouts.finisher: Assault Bike: 1 min max effort — everything you have left. Record calories in 1 min and beat it.
workouts.cooldown: 5 min walk, basic stretch sequence — hamstrings, hip flexors, chest, lats
workouts.progressionNotes: Express sessions: track total workout density (total reps completed in the time). Add reps or reduce rest every 2 weeks. Efficiency is the fitness goal here.

workouts.warmup: 5 min bike easy, leg swings x10, arm circles x20, machine row light x15, leg press light x15

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Safe entry into lower body strength. Control the descent. Don't lock out knees. Good platform for learning leg drive without spinal load.
Machine guides the movement. Focus on feeling the chest. Full ROM. Slow descent. This is your chest builder until free weight pressing is solid.
Pull to chest. Squeeze between shoulder blades. Full range. Machine rows teach the pull pattern safely. Learn to feel your back working.
Dumbbell at chest. Deep and upright. This teaches the real squat pattern beyond what the leg press can. Master this and the barbell squat follows.
Seated. Full ROM. Dumbbells allow natural wrist rotation. Don't press to the point of pain — find your natural groove and stay in it.
Cardiovascular conditioning through the session. Legs then back then arms each stroke. Even, sustainable effort. Build aerobic capacity gradually.

workouts.finisher: Walk on incline treadmill: 8 min at 6-8% grade — low-impact steady state cardiovascular finish
workouts.cooldown: Seated hamstring stretch 45s each, hip flexor stretch 60s each, chest stretch 45s, neck stretch 30s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Beginner machine-based fitness. Progress when 15 reps feels easy for all 3 sets. Transition from machine to free weight equivalents over 8-12 weeks.

workouts.warmup: Jumping jacks x40, hip circles x10, push-up x15, bodyweight squat x20, arm swings x20

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Ascending then descending ladder. Maintain full ROM every rep. As fatigue builds on the descent, form discipline is tested. This is where fitness is made.
Volume through ladder structure. Consistency of form is the standard. At the peak rung, don't rush — maintain plank, maintain depth.
Maximal unilateral leg strength. If pistol squat isn't available, Bulgarian split squat with bodyweight at high reps. Full ROM non-negotiable.
50 total burpees across 5 sets. Paced effort — not explosive start and slow finish. Equal output per set. That's fitness discipline.
Hips level. Drive knees. Breathe. Core and cardiovascular in one. Count reps and aim to hit the same count each round.
Lower body power-endurance. Each jump at max effort. Land softly every time. Soft landing mechanics protect joints and build deceleration strength.

workouts.finisher: Plank hold: 90s — stillness and breath control after high-intensity work. Core composure is fitness too.
workouts.cooldown: 10 min walk if possible, full stretch sequence — quad, hip flexor, hamstring, chest, lat, shoulder
workouts.progressionNotes: Ladder training: track total completion time for the full session. Goal: reduce time by 2-3 min over 4 weeks by improving transitions and rest efficiency.

workouts.warmup: 10 min jog, agility ladder drills (if available), lateral shuffle x10m each, sprint to jog x3

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Reactive power. Explosive hip extension. Soft landing with full foot. Step down. Every rep max intent — not fatigue survivors.
Strength foundation for sport performance. Controlled down, explosive up. Strong squatters are better at almost every sport. Build this.
Horizontal force production. Jump far. Land balanced. Measure and track. Improvement here reflects real athletic development.
Short, maximal sprints. Anaerobic power. Every sprint full effort. Walk the rest fully. Don't turn sprints into tempo runs — that's a different adaptation.
Athletic fitness requires pulling strength. Upper back supports posture under fatigue. Row hard, control the descent.
Multi-directional fitness. Lateral movement is neglected in most gym training. Sink into the working leg. Full hip flexion on the lateral step.

workouts.finisher: Cone drills or Shuttle Run: 5 x 20m, rest 45s between — change-of-direction speed and reactive fitness
workouts.cooldown: 10 min jog, quad stretch 60s each, hip flexor 60s each, hamstring 60s each, calf 45s each
workouts.progressionNotes: Sport fitness: track measurable output monthly. Box jump height, broad jump distance, sprint time. Real fitness shows up in numbers — measure what matters.

workouts.warmup: 5 min bike, dynamic stretch, jumping jacks x30, goblet squat x10, push-up x10

mainWorkout.coachingFocus: Squat into press in one fluid movement. Full depth squat, drive momentum into lockout overhead. The most calorie-efficient single movement in the gym.
Hip snap powers the swing. Not the arms. Breathe with the rhythm of the swing — exhale on the float. 25 reps builds serious work capacity.
Dead hang. Full ROM. In a MetCon context, technique must hold under fatigue. If it breaks, stop that set. Fitness without integrity is injury.
Reactive power in a fatigue environment. This is harder than fresh box jumps — that's the point. Soft landing always. Step down.
250m sprint — all-out effort. Legs then back then arms. Damper on 4-6. Record your time. Sub-55s is strong. Sub-50s is elite.
15 burpees post-sprint is brutal. That's the design. Fitness is built in the uncomfortable gap between wanting to stop and not stopping.

workouts.finisher: AMRAP 5 min: 5 Thrusters + 5 Pull-Ups + 10 Burpees — record rounds completed
workouts.cooldown: 5 min walk, full body stretch, hip flexors 60s each, hamstrings 60s each, child's pose 90s, deep breathing 2 min
workouts.progressionNotes: MetCon sessions: track the AMRAP score. Add 1+ round over 4 weeks. Progress thruster load by 2.5kg monthly. Rowing 250m time is your benchmark — log every sprint.
